title: Swap Two Pointers
hints: Count the stars. `a` is an `int**` (where the caller's `p` lives), `*a` is an `int*` (the caller's `p` itself), `**a` is an `int` (what `p` points at). You are swapping the caller's pointers, so every line should have exactly one star.
It is the three-line swap from problem 2 with the types moved up a level. The temporary holds an address, not an int: `int* t = *a;`. You never need `**`, which is why a null `p` or `q` is harmless.
